form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Manchin (for himself and Mr. Risch) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

form.official-title: To modify the prohibition on financing in the Export-Import Bank of the United States, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Civil Nuclear Export Act of 2023.

section.header: Modification of prohibition on financing in the Export-Import Bank of the United States
section.text: Section 2(b)(5) of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635(b)(5)) is amended, in the first sentence, by inserting , except any purchase that is otherwise permitted under an agreement made in accordance with section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2153) or any other applicable law of the United States, after (C) the purchase.

section.header: Expansion of Program on China and Transformational Exports
section.text: Section 2(l)(1)(B) of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635(l)(1)(B)) is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating clause (xi) as clause (xii); and
by inserting after clause (x) the following:

clause.text: Civil nuclear facilities, material, and technologies, and related goods and services that support the development of an effective nuclear energy sector.

section.text: Section 2 of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635) is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: If there is a claim or judgment against the Bank relating to bodily injury, death, or damage to or loss of real or personal property, the Secretary of the Treasury shall, subject to paragraph (2), pay, from the general fund of the Treasury such claim or judgment, and related costs, if—

subparagraph.text: such bodily injury, death, or damage to or loss of real or personal property is determined in a court of competent jurisdiction to have resulted from a nuclear incident at a nuclear facility that received financial support from the Bank; and
there is no applicable treaty or other arrangement fully absolving the Bank of liability.

paragraph.text: Any claim or judgment, and any related costs paid in accordance with paragraph (1), to the extent not otherwise absolved by any applicable treaty or other arrangement, may not exceed the maximum amount of financial protection per incident required to cover public liability claims under section 170(b) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2210(b)).
If the aggregate amount of claims, judgments, and related costs resulting from a single nuclear incident exceeds the maximum amount under paragraph (2), the President—

subparagraph.text: may authorize, under such terms and conditions as the President may direct, the payment of such claims or judgments, and costs related to such claims or judgments, from any contingency funds available to the United States Government; and
if such funds are insufficient or unavailable, shall certify such claims or judgments to Congress for appropriation of the necessary funds.

section.text: Section 6(a) of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635e(a)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in paragraph (1), by striking applicable amount. and inserting “applicable amount, unless the aggregate amount that is in excess of the applicable amount—

subparagraph.text: is attributed by the Bank to loans, guarantees, and insurance under the Program on China and Transformational Exports pursuant to section 2(l); and
in the header, by striking 2 and inserting 4; and
by striking 2 percent each place it appears and inserting 4 percent; and

paragraph.text: by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.header: Authority to attribute loans, guarantees, and insurance
paragraph.text: The Bank may attribute any loan, guarantee, or insurance issued under the Program on China and Transformational Exports pursuant to section 2(l) toward the aggregate amount that is in excess of the applicable amount described in paragraph (1) without regard to the date on which the Bank issued such loan, guarantee, or insurance.

section.header: Modification of monitoring of default rates
section.text: Section 8(g) of the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 (12 U.S.C. 635g(g)) is amended—

paragraph.text: in paragraph (3), by striking 2 percent each place it appears and inserting 4 percent;
in paragraph (4)(B), by striking 2 percent and inserting 4 percent;

subparagraph.text: in the header, by striking 2 and inserting 4; and
by striking 2 percent and inserting 4 percent;

paragraph.text: in paragraph (6), by striking 2 percent and inserting 4 percent; and
by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.header: Exclusion of transactions relating to the Program on China and Transformational Exports
paragraph.text: For the purposes of this subsection, if financing provided under the Program on China and Transformational Exports pursuant to section 2(l) results in the default rate calculated under paragraph (1) equaling or exceeding 4 percent, the Bank may exclude such financing, subject to the approval of the Board of Directors.
